dominant_strengths: Distinctive torn-paper collage frames the app screenshot, giving Craft a tactile, scrapbook personality that differentiates it from typical SaaS hero shots
Strong serif/italic typographic hook ('your things') anchors the headline with editorial elegance and clear emotional warmth
Pastel sticky-note cards inside the product UI echo the outer paper textures, creating coherent metaphor between marketing and product
dominant_weaknesses: The hero screenshot is awkwardly cropped at the top edge, with paper fragments bleeding into the navbar and feeling more chaotic than curated
Five feature icons sit in a thin monochrome row that feels undersized and visually disconnected from the lush textured hero above
Vertical rhythm between hero, headline, and icon row is loose, leaving a large empty band that weakens narrative flow on scroll
fix_priorities: Tighten hero crop and balance the torn-paper collage so navbar elements aren't visually competing with overlapping textures
Elevate the feature icon row with labels typography hierarchy, subtle dividers or cards to match the hero's craft level
Reduce vertical whitespace between headline and icon row, or introduce a transitional element to bind the two sections
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral leads via tactile paper textures and warm palette, reflective follows through the playful brand voice, but behavioral clarity lags as the icon row feels generic.
rationale.intent_fit: Effectively communicates Craft as a versatile, characterful Mac doc app, though the scroll section's composition undersells its own craft.
